UNITED STATES TAX COURT
Washington, D.C.

MICHAEL A. OKAFOR and DIANE R. OKAFOR,
                              Petitioners,
        v.                                          Docket No. _____-25
COMMISSIONER OF INTERNAL REVENUE,
                              Respondent.

PETITION
(Filed June 30, 2025, pursuant to Tax Court Rule 34 and IRC Section 6213(a))

Petitioners hereby petition for a redetermination of the deficiency set forth by the Commissioner
of Internal Revenue in the Notice of Deficiency dated April 7, 2025, for the taxable year 2022,
and as grounds for their case allege as follows:

1. Petitioners are individuals residing in Cary, North Carolina, and filed a joint federal income
   tax return for 2022.

2. The Notice of Deficiency determined a deficiency of $17,850 and an accuracy-related penalty of
   $3,570 under IRC Section 6662(a).

3. Petitioners assign the following errors:

   (a) Respondent erred in determining that $47,600 in bank deposits constituted unreported gross
       receipts. Petitioners will show that $23,200 of the deposits identified were transfers from
       the Okafors' own joint savings account (already-taxed funds moved between the couple's own
       accounts) and $14,000 represented repayment of a personal loan Petitioner Michael Okafor
       made to Gerald T. Wynn in 2021, which is a nontaxable return of principal, not income.

   (b) Respondent erred in disallowing in full the claimed vehicle, home office, and contract
       labor expenses. Petitioners will produce a partial contemporaneous mileage log and
       corrected home-office square-footage calculation to substantiate a portion of these
       expenses under IRC Section 162(a).

   (c) In the alternative, Petitioner Diane R. Okafor requests relief from joint and several
       liability under IRC Section 6015(b), (c), and/or (f) (innocent spouse relief) on the
       grounds that she had no involvement in, and no reason to know of, the underreporting of
       income attributable to Okafor Strategic Consulting, a business operated exclusively by
       Petitioner Michael A. Okafor.

   (d) Respondent erred in asserting the accuracy-related penalty under IRC Section 6662(a).
       Petitioners had reasonable cause and acted in good faith, including reliance on their
       return preparer, within the meaning of IRC Section 6664(c).

4. Petitioners further note that pursuant to IRC Section 7491(a), the burden of proof as to the
   unreported income adjustment shifts to Respondent because Petitioners fully cooperated with
   the examination and maintain that credible evidence has been introduced with respect to the
   disputed factual issues.

WHEREFORE, Petitioners pray that this Court:
  (a) redetermine that there is no deficiency in income tax due from Petitioners for 2022, or in
      the alternative a substantially reduced deficiency;
  (b) redetermine that Diane R. Okafor is relieved of joint and several liability;
  (c) redetermine that no accuracy-related penalty is due; and
  (d) grant such other relief as the Court deems just.

/s/ Renata Alvarez-Kim
Counsel for Petitioners
